overview: The Medford Promote, Prevent, Support Behavioral Health Commission met remotely to review school-based mental health partnerships, discuss program mapping and data collection strategies across city departments, and receive community outreach updates. The commission approved the prior meeting's minutes and welcomed a new municipal recovery coach.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the March 2, 2022 meeting.

items.title: School Updates on Behavioral Health Programming Care
items.summary: Stacey Schulman detailed the Medford Public Schools partnership with Care Solace to connect students, families, and staff with mental health and substance use providers, noting high demand for anxiety and depression care alongside a regional shortage of available clinicians.

items.title: Subcommittee Reports: Planning and Program & Data Collection
items.summary: The commission reviewed plans to inventory local behavioral health programs using a standardized form and discussed aggregating non-identifiable, department-level data to identify community needs and service gaps.

items.title: Communities That Care Youth Survey Update
items.summary: Penny Funaiole updated the commission on the winter 2021 youth survey administration, language translation efforts for English learner students, and upcoming data analysis with the statistician.

items.title: Office of Prevention Outreach Updates and Announcements
items.summary: The commission introduced new recovery coach Jeff Gibson and shared available professional development trainings, upcoming criminal justice webinars, and the schedule for the next meeting.
